title: Structural Genome Annotation QC with GAQET2
author: Victor Garcia-Carpintero

steps.title: Prepare Input Files
steps.instruction: Gather the necessary files required for the Structural Genome Annotation (SGA) quality assessment.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the genome assembly in FASTA format.
Obtain the SGA annotation file in GTF or GFF3 format.
Optional: Provide proteome files in FASTA format for homology search (e.g., TrEMBL and SWISSPROT from uniprot.org).
Optional: Download the Ortholog MAtrix (OMA) database file (.h5) from the OMArk github or omabrowser.org for taxonomic consistency and completeness analyses.

steps.title: Create YAML Configuration File
steps.instruction: Create a YAML configuration file to define the GAQET run parameters.

substeps.instruction: Set 'ID' (Species Name), 'Assembly' (path to FASTA), 'Annotation' (path to GFF3/GTF), and 'Basedir' (results directory).
Specify 'Threads' for processing.
Define 'Analysis' as a list of tools to run (options: AGAT, BUSCO, PSAURON, DETENGA, OMARK, PROTHOMOLOGY).
If OMARK is selected: Provide 'OMARK_db' (path to .h5 file) and 'OMARK_taxid' (NCBI taxon ID).
If BUSCO is selected: Provide 'BUSCO_lineages' (list of clade identifiers from busco.ezlab.org, excluding the date part of the name).
If PROTHOMOLOGY is selected: Provide 'PROTHOMOLOGY_tags' as a list of user-defined names and paths to DIAMOND protein databases.
If DETENGA is selected: Specify 'DETENGA_db' (choices: 'rexdb-plant', 'rexdb-metazoa', or 'rexdb').

steps.title: Run GAQET Analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the GAQET program using the configuration file.

substeps.instruction: Run the basic command: `GAQET --YAML <config_file>`.
Alternatively, use command-line arguments to override YAML settings: `-s` (species ID), `-g` (genome), `-a` (annotation), `-t` (taxid), and `-o` (outbase).
Example for multiple species: `GAQET -i GAQET_PLANTS.yaml -s <Species_Name> -o <Results_Dir> -g <Genome_File> -a <Annotation_File> -t <TaxID>`.

steps.title: Verify Results and Logs
steps.instruction: Review the output directory and log files to ensure the analysis completed successfully.

substeps.instruction: Check the output folder for analysis-specific directories (AGAT_run, BUSCOCompleteness_run, DETENGA_run, DIAMOND_run, OMARK_run, PSAURON_run).
Inspect `GAQET.log.txt` for binary availability checks, reformatting details, and run errors.
Locate the summary results in the `{species}_GAQET.stats.tsv` file.

steps.title: Prepare Data for Visualization
steps.instruction: Prepare the metrics summary files for plotting.

substeps.instruction: Use a single `{species}_GAQET.stats.tsv` file for one annotation.
For comparing multiple annotations, merge the summary files into a single stats file by adding rows for each summary to be compared.

steps.title: Generate GAQET Plot
steps.instruction: Run the GAQET_PLOT tool to create a visual representation of the QC metrics.

substeps.instruction: Execute the command: `GAQET_PLOT -i <input_stats_file> -o <output_filename>`, ensuring the output filename has a `.png` or `.svg` suffix.

steps.title: Interpret QC Results
steps.instruction: Analyze the generated plot and stats file to evaluate annotation quality.

substeps.instruction: Review the Inner Radar Plot for global percentage metrics and the Inner Ring for the overall quality area score (higher is better).

Analyze Outer Column sets for: BUSCO completeness (% Complete Single), Transposons (% potential TEs via DeTEnGA), Gene/Transcript model counts, % Transcripts with both side UTRs, and Average CDS length.
Cross-reference the `{species}_TE_summary.csv` file for specific sequence IDs flagged as TEs by DeTEnGA.
